title: Lesson Cards Stop Faking Pictures With Emoji | vitalii.no
description:
Lesson cards for kids needed to draw a honeycomb, but the card writer had no way to actually draw one — so it grabbed the nearest emoji instead, a honey pot standing in for a honeycomb. Every effect on a card invented its own one-off way of showing a picture, so there was no shared scale, and a near-miss emoji could teach a kid the wrong thing.

I built a shared drawing kit in drawSpec.js: primitives like polygons, grids, bars, icons and groups, plus actions like count, highlight, split and compare, all computed at one shared true scale. The same drawSpec.js output feeds both the on-screen renderer and the automated content checker, so the picture shown and the picture checked can never disagree. When no picture exists that actually matches a word, the content gate now refuses the card outright instead of falling back to a lookalike.

Every picture slot across the lesson format — stations, split-compare, sort-into-bins, bins, the magnifier target and reveal-answer — now draws from the same real kit instead of guessing with emoji. All 6 slot types draw the real thing.
